downstream_consequence.note: At ROLE level the lane mixes are similar, yet per family they diverge sharply (atom_insert 16.3% synthetic in train against 95.2% in validation). The 16 validation shards mine different family x lane combinations, so shard implies cohort implies family mix, lane mix and teacher policy together. This is the upstream source of the provenance shift measured earlier.

implication_for_the_refreeze: Reserving more real sources from the validation ROLE cannot fix this -- every validation source sits in those same 16 shards. A population-matched panel must be carved from WITHIN the 270 training shards, source-disjoint. Whether that is safe depends on whether a shard is an analogue series (in which case within-shard holdout leaks near relatives) or a diverse sample; splitting by shard is the standard defence against exactly that leakage, so the trade-off must be measured rather than assumed.

precedence_is_not_the_cause.note: Our resolution moved almost nothing; roles were already disjoint upstream.

question: The exposure diagnostic localized the residual real-lane gap to the boundary between training-role and validation-role sources -- both unseen, so a population effect rather than a learning one. What separates the populations?
recommended_evaluation_design: Primary validation for checkpoint selection: source-disjoint holdout carved from within the 270 training shards, stratified by lane, family and capability cell, sized to give atom_insert and atom_delete real coverage.
Secondary: retain the present 16-shard panel explicitly labelled as a cross-cohort / OOD stress test, not as ordinary validation.

root_cause.finding: partition_role is assigned PER TASK SHARD, not per source. Validation is 16 specific upstream mining shards with zero overlap against the 270 training shards, so it is a different mining cohort by construction and cannot be a neutral sample of the training population. The unseen_source -> held_out boundary IS a shard boundary.
